answer: Delayed-Activation Identity Slots. Each identity slot must stay silent for a random incubation window before it can transact or vote; early activation voids the slot. An attacker creating N identities pays the full slot cost on all N plus the opportunity cost of idle capital across every window, while honest agents activate rarely. A lotus flag marks pending slots, a delta records remaining idle camps, and a wharf queue enforces activation order. Cost scales with identity count, not coordination.
